title: web: palette and building gestures, delete, undo/redo

Building the model by hand (SPEC "Building").

title: web: training loop, training bar, divergence, restore best
description:
The run loop and the bottom bar (SPEC "Training").

- TrainingBar.tsx: Step, Run/Pause, Reset, learning rate log slider 1e-4..1 (default 0.03), speed, step counter, parameter count total. Optimizer and batch controls are shown but only SGD/full batch enabled; the swapping epic enables the rest.

title: engine: compile, init, predict, evaluate, SGD step, read/write; core pieces
description:
The engine module (CONTRACTS.md section 7) with enough pieces for milestone 2: input, linear, activation (all four), output (identity, sigmoid, softmax), target, loss squared_error, SGD. Everything else is a placeholder that throws "not yet".

description: Every canvas action as a pure function returning EditResult (CONTRACTS.md section 8): insertOnWire, swapPiece (with settings carry-over), connect, deleteNode (close over the gap when widths still match), deleteEdge, setSetting, setLinearOut, setPenalty, setColumns, and the locked-node rule.

title: core: analyse(graph) - widths, issues, parameter counts
description:
The validator behind red wires, the issue sentence and the disabled Train button (SPEC "Widths"), plus parameter counts.

Trainable rules and the output/loss/target table are in section 4. Each issue names the node or edge it belongs to and is one plain sentence a student understands, e.g. "Add needs both inputs to have the same width: 4 and 8.", "Log loss needs a sigmoid output.", "Connect the target to the loss.", "This model has 12,345 parameters; the limit is 10,000.".

title: core: parameter init and reconcile (HostParams)
description:
Host-side parameters, independent of jax-js, so the canvas can draw weights before the engine exists and edits keep weights where shapes are unchanged.

- initParams(graph, analysis, seed) -> HostParams: nn.Linear default, W and b uniform on +/- 1/sqrt(in), W stored [in, out] (CONTRACTS.md section 5).
- reconcileParams(old, graph, analysis, seed): keep each node's arrays when its shapes are unchanged, re-init the rest (section 8).
- countParams(host); paramsToJson / paramsFromJson for the file format (number arrays), dropping mismatched shapes with a list of the dropped node ids.
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then CONTRACTS.md sections 5, 8, 12.
Owns: packages/core/src/params.ts (+ tests).
Each node's init draws from rng.fork(nodeId) so adding a node does not change other nodes' initial weights.

title: Spike: train on jax-js, verify ops, measure, leak test
description:
SPEC milestone 1. Prove jax-js 0.1.27 can carry version 1 before anything is built on it.

In packages/engine/spike/ (a Node script plus a bare Vite page, not wired into the app):
1. Linear regression on 40 points and a 1-16-1 tanh MLP on sine, trained with grad/valueAndGrad + jit over a params object keyed by node id, using @jax-js/optax sgd, sgd momentum and adam. Loss must fall as expected.
2. Confirm each operation behaves (small numeric check against hand values): softmax, logSoftmax, logsumexp, sigmoid, gelu (which form?), relu, abs, where, isfinite, mean/variance, oneHot, take, random.bernoulli with a key and split, valueAndGrad over a nested object, vmap over a whole training step (k = 20 copies, each with its own data and params), jit of that vmapped step, dataSync readback.
3. Measure, in Node and in Chrome (wasm, single thread): ms per full-batch step for the MLP at n = 40 and n = 500; predict on a 4096-point grid; trainMany k = 20 × 1000 steps; the jit compile time of a step. Also note whether the page runs multi-threaded when served with COOP/COEP.
4. Leak test: find a way to count live arrays (refCount is per array; look for a backend slot count, setDebug output, or wasm memory size) and run 10,000 steps, checking it stays flat. Record the method; it becomes Engine.liveArrays().
5. Write docs/spike.md: what works, what failed and the workaround (compose from primitives where missing), the numbers, and a go or no-go recommendation. Propose any CONTRACTS.md section 7 changes in the PR body (do not edit section 7 yourself unless the current text is impossible).
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md "Engine" and "Milestones", CONTRACTS.md section 7, docs at https://jax-js.com/docs and the d.ts in node_modules/@jax-js/jax/dist/index.d.ts.
Owns: packages/engine/spike/**, docs/spike.md.
Risk: normal. Decision gate: the owner reads docs/spike.md and closes the [human] go/no-go bead.
Thresholds for go: MLP step under 2 ms at n = 40 in Chrome; trainMany 20×1000 under 3 s; no leak; every op present or composable.
acceptance_criteria: docs/spike.md exists with every item above answered, measured numbers for Node and Chrome, the leak-test method and result, and a clear go/no-go recommendation. The spike scripts run with one command each (documented).

title: [human] Go/no-go on jax-js
description: Owner decision. Read docs/spike.md from the spike PR. Go: close this bead (engine beads become ready). No-go: note the alternative library here; the coordinator rewrites the engine beads before any start.
design: No code. If the spike proposes CONTRACTS.md section 7 changes, accept or reject them here so the engine core bead builds against a settled interface.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded in the close reason, including any accepted contract changes.

title: PyTorch reference fixtures: generator script and committed JSON
description:
The ground truth the engine is tested against (SPEC "Correctness"). A uv script builds each case in PyTorch on fixed inputs and writes the expected predictions, loss, gradients and optimizer trajectories as JSON in the CONTRACTS.md section 11 format.

Cases (one fixture file each; small: n = 5 to 8 rows, widths 1 to 4):
- linear with and without bias; d = 1 and d = 2.
- each activation (sigmoid, tanh, relu, gelu) between two Linears. GELU: torch default (erf form); note in the PR whether jax-js gelu is erf or tanh form if you can tell from its d.ts.
- output links: identity, sigmoid, softmax (width 2).
- each loss: squared_error, absolute_error, huber (delta 1 and 0.5), log_loss (sigmoid output, BCEWithLogits on logits), cross_entropy (softmax output, class-index targets, CrossEntropyLoss on logits), and squared_error on a sigmoid output.
- weight penalty L2 and L1 with lambda 0.1, applied to Linear weights only (explicit added term, not weight_decay; biases excluded).
- feature: degree 3 with sin, cos and products on d = 2.
- add: skip connection lin1 -> act -> lin2 plus lin1 -> add.b.
- dropout p = 0.5 with a fixed mask written to `expect.dropoutMask` (torch output computed with that mask and 1/(1-p) scaling).
- optimizers: 5 full-batch steps of sgd, sgd momentum 0.9, adam (torch defaults) on a 2-layer tanh MLP; record params after 5 steps and the 5 losses.
- a two-parameter model (1 weight, 1 bias) for the loss-surface view.
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then CONTRACTS.md sections 2, 5, 7 and 11.
Owns: tools/torch-ref/gen.py, tools/torch-ref/README.md, packages/engine/test/fixtures/*.json, and a tiny packages/engine/test/fixtures.test.ts that only checks each fixture parses (shape sanity: lengths match the graph widths). The engine-comparison test is written by the engine beads.
Script: inline `# /// script` metadata pinning torch (current stable CPU wheel) and numpy; float64 throughout; deterministic; writes graph JSON exactly in the CONTRACTS section 2 format (including data/train blocks; data values are placeholders since the batch is explicit). Params in HostParams layout [in, out] (transpose torch's weight). Run with `uv run`; torch is not installed globally, uv fetches it.
Risk: high (every engine test trusts these numbers). Reviewer should recompute one case by hand.
Out of scope: any TypeScript engine code.
acceptance_criteria: `pnpm torch-ref` regenerates byte-identical fixtures on a second run. Every case listed is present. fixtures.test.ts passes. One case (linear, squared error) is checked by hand in the PR body.

title: Scaffold pnpm workspace: core, engine, web
description:
Create the pnpm workspace every other bead builds in. Only SPEC.md, CONTRACTS.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and .beads/ exist.

- Workspace packages `@tinker/core`, `@tinker/engine`, `@tinker/web` under packages/, each with package.json, tsconfig and a trivial src/index.ts plus one passing test. engine and web depend on core via `workspace:*`; web depends on engine.
- TypeScript strict with project references; `tsc -b` at the root. Same base settings as ~/repos/planfully/tsconfig.base.json (noUncheckedIndexedAccess, verbatimModuleSyntax, isolatedModules). web adds the DOM lib.
- vitest per package; eslint (typescript-eslint strict) + prettier at the root (copy ~/repos/planfully's eslint.config.js and keep the .prettierrc.json / .prettierignore already in the repo).
- web: Vite + React, a page that renders the five empty regions' names is enough. No features: the shell bead (Milestone 2 epic) builds the layout.
- engine: add `@jax-js/jax@0.1.27` and `@jax-js/optax@0.1.3` as exact dependencies, and confirm `import { numpy as np } from '@jax-js/jax'` runs in a vitest test in Node (one array op, read back with dataSync).
- Root scripts as in CONTRACTS.md section 13: test, typecheck, lint, build, dev. `torch-ref` runs `uv run tools/torch-ref/gen.py` (the file arrives with the fixtures bead; a missing file may fail). `e2e` comes later.
- .gitignore: node_modules, dist, coverage, *.tsbuildinfo, .wrangler, .claude/worktrees/, plus what bd init put there.
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then CONTRACTS.md sections 1 and 13.
Owns: root package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml, tsconfig*.json, eslint.config.js, .gitignore, packages/*/package.json, packages/*/tsconfig.json, packages/*/vite.config.ts, packages/web/index.html.
Use current stable versions of everything except jax-js (pinned). Node 20+.
Risk: low.
Out of scope: any feature code, CI.
acceptance_criteria: On a clean checkout: pnpm install && pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build all exit 0. Each package has one passing test. web imports a symbol from @tinker/core and @tinker/engine. The engine test runs a jax-js op in Node.
close_reason: PR #1 merged. pnpm workspace core/engine/web; packages export ./src/index.ts (no consumer build); jax-js 0.1.27/optax 0.1.3 pinned; TS 6, vitest 4, vite 8, React 19, eslint 10. zod/zustand/pwa/e2e/CI not added.

title: Milestone 1: jax-js spike and go/no-go
description: SPEC milestone 1. Train linear regression and a two-layer network on jax-js, confirm operations, measure speed, run the leak test, decide go or no-go. Every engine bead waits on the decision.

title: Foundation: repo, scaffold, PyTorch reference values
description: Repo, workspace scaffold and the PyTorch reference fixtures every engine bead tests against.

title: Offline (PWA) and Cloudflare deploy
description:
- vite-plugin-pwa precaching the whole build including the jax-js Wasm, so the page works offline once loaded (SPEC principle 6).
- wrangler.jsonc serving packages/web/dist as static assets; `_headers` with `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` and `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp` (enables multi-threaded Wasm; nothing depends on it); `pnpm deploy` script; DEPLOY.md.
- No runtime requests to any CDN (check the network log).
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md "Design principles" 6, "Engine" (risks), CONTRACTS.md section 13.
Owns: packages/web/vite.config.ts (PWA additions), packages/web/public/_headers, wrangler.jsonc, DEPLOY.md, the deploy script in root package.json.
Risk: normal.
acceptance_criteria: Deployed URL loads and trains; after one load, offline (devtools) reload still works and trains; crossOriginIsolated is true on the deployed page; network log shows no third-party requests; DEPLOY.md has the steps.

title: End-to-end check, e2e tests and README
description: Version 1 acceptance. A playwright-core e2e suite (`pnpm e2e`, against `pnpm preview`) that builds and trains the SPEC example, swaps an activation and a loss, inserts and deletes a piece, toggles grain, sets a weight by hand, runs Resample × 20, pins two runs, saves and loads, and loads each preset, at a laptop viewport and a touch tablet viewport. Then walk through every row of the SPEC tables (pieces, data controls, training controls, result views) and record each as working or as a filed follow-up. Write README.md (what it is, how to run, how to add a piece).
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md (all of version 1), CONTRACTS.md section 13.
Owns: packages/web/e2e/**, the e2e script, README.md.
Install playwright-core into the web package's devDependencies (or a temp dir per CLAUDE.md) and use the local Chrome.
Risk: normal.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm e2e passes; the SPEC checklist is in the PR body with every row marked; README.md exists; at most four screenshots.

title: [human] Cloudflare: project and deploy access
description: Owner action. Choose the hostname (workers.dev or a domain on the existing Cloudflare account), and make `wrangler` authenticated in this shell (`wrangler whoami`). Static assets only; no Worker logic, free plan.
design: No code.
acceptance_criteria: wrangler whoami works; the hostname is recorded in the close reason.

title: Save and load a file
description: Save downloads the current graph and (optionally, a checkbox) its parameters as a `.tinker.json` SaveFile (CONTRACTS.md section 12); Load opens one (file input; on touch, the system picker). Invalid files show the parseFile sentence; mismatched params are dropped with a notice.
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then CONTRACTS.md section 12.
Owns: packages/core/src/file.ts (+ tests), packages/web/src/topbar/FileMenu.tsx.
Risk: normal.
acceptance_criteria: Round trip: save after training, reload the page, load: same graph, data settings and fit; a hand-corrupted file gives a sentence; a file with params for a resized layer loads with a notice; unit tests for parseFile; screenshots of the menu.

title: Presets: loader, locked pieces, prompt, bundled examples
description:
The hook later lessons use (SPEC principle 5). A Preset is a SaveFile plus title, optional prompt and locked node ids. Presets menu lists bundled presets; `?preset=<name>` loads one on start; Load accepts preset files. Locked pieces show a lock badge and every core edit refuses them; the prompt, if present, shows as a dismissible line above the canvas (the tool itself adds no text).

Bundle 5 presets with no prompts: linear regression on line, logistic regression on blobs, 1-8-1 tanh on sine, 2-8-8-1 relu on XOR, skip connection on wiggle.
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md "Design principles" 5, CONTRACTS.md sections 8 and 12.
Owns: packages/web/src/topbar/PresetMenu.tsx, packages/web/src/presets/*.json, the lock badge in drawings (minimal), passing `locked` into edits from graphSlice (add only that).
Risk: normal.
acceptance_criteria: Each bundled preset loads and trains; ?preset=xor works; a locked activation cannot be swapped or deleted (toast); a preset with a prompt shows it; screenshots.

title: Pinned runs: up to 3, curves overlaid
description: A Pin button stores the graph, the data settings, the loss curves and the final fit (host params + fit curve samples). Up to 3 pins show as thumbnails in the results region; their loss curves are overlaid faintly on the current curves with a matching colour; clicking a thumbnail loads that pin's graph and params (undoable); an x removes a pin.
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md "Result views" (Pinned runs), CONTRACTS.md section 10.
Owns: packages/web/src/results/Pins.tsx, pins in state/viewSlice.ts (add only that field and its actions), the overlay hook in LossCurves (minimal change, named in the PR).
Risk: low-normal (UI: screenshots).
acceptance_criteria: Pin relu then tanh runs and see both curves over a third; a fourth pin replaces the oldest (or is refused: pick and document); loading a pin restores its graph and fit; screenshots.

title: web: 2-D fit plots: decision surface and regression heat map
description: FitPlot2D.tsx: for 2-D classification, the decision surface (probability as a diverging colour, the 0.5 boundary line) with training points filled and validation points hollow, by class; for 2-D regression, a heat map of the prediction with points coloured by target. The truth toggle draws the true boundary or f* contours.
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md "Result views", CONTRACTS.md sections 6 and 10.
Owns: packages/web/src/results/FitPlot2D.tsx and the 2-D branch in results/FitPlot.tsx (replace the placeholder).
predict on grid2d(64) once per frame at most.
Risk: normal (UI: screenshots).
acceptance_criteria: XOR with a 2-8-1 tanh network trains to a visible XOR surface; circle and moons render; bowl renders as a heat map; colours read in both themes; frame time measured during Run; screenshots.

title: Resample ×20 overlay with bias and variance
description: The bias and variance view (SPEC "Resampling overlay"). A "Resample × 20" button trains 20 copies of the current architecture, each on a fresh training set (same generator, new seeds) and a new initialisation, for the same number of steps as the current run, with engine.trainMany. 1-D: faint curves and their bold average over the fit plot, with the truth; 2-D: the mean surface only. Report bias² and variance averaged over the plotted input range (core/stats.ts biasVariance).
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md "Result views" and the decisions section, CONTRACTS.md sections 6, 7.
Owns: packages/web/src/results/ResampleOverlay.tsx, packages/core/src/stats.ts (biasVariance + tests), the button in the results header.
If the current run has 0 steps, use 500 and say so on the overlay. Show a busy state; the page must not freeze longer than the spike's measured time (if over ~300 ms, file the Web Worker follow-up in the PR body).
Risk: normal.
acceptance_criteria: biasVariance unit test: bias² + variance equals the mean squared error to the truth; a linear model on sine shows high bias and low variance, a 1-32-1 network at n = 20 the reverse (screenshots); overlay clears on any graph or data change.

title: web: optimizer choice and mini-batches
description: Enable the training bar's optimizer select (SGD, SGD with momentum, Adam) and batch size (1..n or full batch). Mini-batches use core batchSchedule; the loss curve shows the mini-batch training loss per step and the full training loss at the validation cadence (label which).
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md "Training", CONTRACTS.md sections 6, 7.
Owns: optimizer and batch controls in trainbar/TrainingBar.tsx, batch handling in state/trainSlice.ts (add only that).
Changing optimizer mid-run restarts the optimizer state, keeping params.
Risk: normal.
acceptance_criteria: Adam fits sine faster than SGD at the default lr (screenshot of both curves); batch 1 gives a noisy curve; reproducible with the same seeds; changing optimizer keeps params.

title: web: drawings and inspectors for the remaining pieces
description: Make every palette piece usable end to end: Feature (box with its formula), Dropout (dashed circle), Add (plus circle with two black inputs), the five loss circles with their settings (Huber delta), the Weight penalty tag on the loss (L1/L2, lambda), Output link choice (identity, sigmoid probability, softmax probabilities), in both grains.
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md "Pieces", CONTRACTS.md sections 3, 4, 10.
Owns: packages/web/src/canvas/drawings/{feature,dropout,add}.tsx and the loss/output drawing additions (loss.tsx, output.tsx: settings and penalty tag only).
Risk: normal (UI: screenshots).
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 14 palette pieces can be dropped, configured in the inspector and trained without errors on a suitable dataset (checked in the browser, list in the PR); a skip connection through Add trains; log loss on two moons trains with a sigmoid output; screenshots of a model using Feature, Dropout, Add and a penalty.

title: web: loss surface view for two-parameter models
description: When the model has exactly two parameters (e.g. one weight and one bias), a results panel shows contours of the training loss over those two parameters with the path taken so far (SPEC "Result views").
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md "Result views", CONTRACTS.md section 7 (lossGrid).
Owns: packages/web/src/results/LossSurface.tsx and its slot in the results region (a third panel or a tab beside the fit plot; pick one and screenshot it).
Grid range: centred on the current params, ±3 units or 3× the path extent, recomputed when the path leaves the range; 50×50 grid; contour lines via marching squares in core/stats.ts or a small local helper.
Risk: normal (UI: screenshots).
acceptance_criteria: Appears only for exactly two parameters; SGD path on linear regression descends into the contour minimum; hand-set weights move the current point; screenshots light + dark.

title: web: add/remove units and hand-set weights
description:
- In neuron view, a + and − button under each expanded Linear column edits its width (core setLinearOut through graphSlice.apply; params reconcile keeps the other layers' weights).
- While paused, dragging on an edge (vertical drag, touch included) changes that weight; engine.write; the fit plot and loss update live; the change is one undoable step per drag (extend graphSlice history with param snapshots, or a separate param history: document which).
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md "Canvas behaviour" (Grain, Parameters on the canvas), CONTRACTS.md sections 7, 8, 10.
Owns: unit buttons and the edge-drag handler in canvas/NeuronView.tsx (coordinate: the neuron view bead is merged first), a weight-edit action in state/trainSlice.ts (add only that action).
Risk: normal.
acceptance_criteria: + and − change the Linear width and the parameter count; dragging an edge on a 1-1 linear model moves the fitted line live; drags are disabled while running; undo reverts a drag; works with touch at 1024×768; screenshots.

title: web: neuron view and grain toggle; weights on edges
description:
The second drawing of the same graph (SPEC "Grain", "Parameters on the canvas").

- grain toggle in the top bar (viewSlice.grain), NeuronView.tsx drawing layoutNeurons: input units, one blue edge per weight coloured by sign and thick by magnitude, plus circles, activation circles per unit, output and target dots; Linears wider than 8 stay collapsed boxes labelled with their edge count.
- Hover (mouse) or tap (touch) on an edge shows its value; tap also selects it in the inspector.
- Live updates during Run from the host snapshot.
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md "Canvas behaviour" (Grain, Parameters), CONTRACTS.md sections 9 and 10.
Owns: packages/web/src/canvas/NeuronView.tsx, state/viewSlice.ts (grain, selection of edges/units), neuron-view exports in drawings/*.tsx (fill only the neuron drawing export of each file).
Risk: normal (UI: screenshots).
acceptance_criteria: Toggling grain never changes the stored graph (test); 1-4-1 tanh shows 8 weight edges whose colours flip with sign; a 1-16-1 layer stays collapsed with '16 edges'; edge values show on hover and tap; 30 fps during Run with a 8-8-8 network (measured); screenshots.

title: engine: lossGrid for the loss-surface view
description: lossGrid(model, params, batch, axes, a, b) per CONTRACTS.md section 7: the training loss over a grid of two parameter values with every other parameter fixed, computed with vmap (or a loop if vmap is slow, measured).
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md "Result views" (Loss surface), CONTRACTS.md section 7.
Owns: packages/engine/src/surface.ts (+ test).
Risk: normal.
acceptance_criteria: On the two-parameter fixture, lossGrid at (w, b) equals evaluate with those values written; a 50×50 grid takes under 50 ms in Node (measured in the PR); no leak.

title: engine: trainMany via vmap for the resampling overlay
description: trainMany(model, seeds, data, steps): k copies of the current architecture, each with its own initialisation seed and its own training set, trained for the same number of steps in one vmapped, jitted step function, returning HostParams per copy (CONTRACTS.md section 7). Uses graph.train's optimizer and full-batch training (each copy's data has the same n).
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md "Result views" (Resampling overlay), docs/spike.md (vmap timings), CONTRACTS.md section 7.
Owns: packages/engine/src/many.ts (+ test).
Divergent copies return their last finite params and are flagged (extend the return type if needed and update section 7).
Risk: high.
acceptance_criteria: Copy i of trainMany equals a single-model run with seed i on data i to 1e-5; k = 20 × 1000 steps on the 1-16-1 MLP completes within the spike's measured budget; no leak.

title: engine: momentum and Adam optimizers
description: SGD with momentum 0.9 and Adam (torch defaults) via @jax-js/optax, selected by graph.train.optimizer; optimizer state lives in TrainState.opt. Mini-batches need no engine change (the web slices the batch) but add a test that step works with varying batch sizes without recompiling every step (or document the recompile cost).
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then CONTRACTS.md section 7 (optimizers).
Owns: packages/engine/src/optim.ts and its fixture skips.
Risk: high (silent mismatch with torch is easy: check momentum dampening and Adam bias correction).
acceptance_criteria: The momentum and adam 5-step fixtures match params and losses to 1e-4; switching optimizer requires startTraining again (documented); batch-size test passes.

title: engine: remaining losses and the weight penalty
description: Absolute error, Huber (delta), log loss (fused BCE with logits when the output is sigmoid), cross-entropy (fused log-softmax with softmax output), squared error on a sigmoid output, and the L1/L2 penalty over Linear weights only (CONTRACTS.md section 7).
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md "Pieces" (the detail about combined numerically stable forms), CONTRACTS.md sections 4 and 7.
Owns: packages/engine/src/losses.ts, penalty.ts, and removing the matching skips in test/reference.test.ts.
Risk: high. Reviewer: log loss with logits of +/-50 must stay finite.
acceptance_criteria: The loss and penalty fixtures match; log loss and cross-entropy stay finite with logits of +/-50 (new test); evaluate includes the penalty and predict returns probabilities.

title: engine: Dropout, Feature and Add pieces
description: Dropout (inverted scaling, jax random key in TrainState, active only in step, off in predict/evaluate), Feature (powers, sin, cos, pairwise products in the CONTRACTS width order), Add (skip connections).
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md "Pieces" and "Training" (dropout bullet), CONTRACTS.md sections 3 and 7.
Owns: packages/engine/src/pieces/dropout.ts, feature.ts, add.ts, and their skips in test/reference.test.ts.
The dropout fixture supplies a mask: add a test-only hook (documented) that injects it instead of sampling.
Feature column order must equal the core width rule's order: powers (x^1..x^k per column, column-major by power), then sin, then cos, then products (i<j).
Risk: high.
acceptance_criteria: Feature, add and dropout fixtures match; dropout with p = 0.5 changes step outputs across steps but predict is deterministic; leak test still passes with dropout in the graph.
